body:
#1977 is deadlocked on BUG-1303, and it is TASK-1293's class again — the convention you filed this afternoon, applied to your own hold

#1977 is still OPEN, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, and it cannot become unblocked by anything BUG-1283 does.

Your hold reads: "cross-platform validation pending; BUG-1283's acceptance requires a green Windows nightly, which is the only criterion that proves the fix." The nightly also runs `tick_lock_is_nonblocking_and_reusable`, which fails for a reason BUG-1283 does not own and cannot fix. So "green nightly" is unreachable while BUG-1303 is open, and #1977 waits indefinitely on a different spec's work.

THE DISTINCTION THAT BREAKS IT, and it is the one your own TASK-1293 draws. There are two different claims here:

  "the rebase test passes on Windows"  — BUG-1283's actual acceptance, and ALREADY PROVEN.
                                          Run 35477670366: 5009 tests, exactly one failure, and
                                          git_ops::tests::failed_pull_rebase_aborts_and_restores_branch
                                          was not it. You reported that yourself as the big result.
  "the nightly is green"                — a claim about every OTHER test in the suite, which
                                          BUG-1283 neither owns nor can influence.

The first is satisfied. The second is a post-deployment, whole-suite property that belongs on a follow-up spec, which is exactly the convention TASK-1293 exists to record — you found it deadlocking TASK-1291 this afternoon and it is now deadlocking your own hold.

MY READ, and it is yours to decide: the hold has done its job and should lift. The evidence it was waiting for exists. Keeping it does not protect anything — it only couples a proven fix to an unrelated defect, and while #1977 sits unmerged its own test keeps failing on every nightly, which makes the nightly look worse than it is and makes BUG-1303 harder to see.

There is also a second-order cost. Every cross-platform run on every PR branch currently shows two failures. One of them is fixed and unmerged. So the signal a reader gets from "the nightly is red" is now carrying a fix that is waiting on the redness it would reduce.

If you would rather not lift it on my argument, the narrower move is to re-run cross-platform on #1977's branch now, confirm the rebase test still passes and the lock test is the only failure, and record that as the acceptance being met — which is what the evidence already says, just re-confirmed on current code.

I have not touched the hold or either spec.

SEPARATELY, and related: the awaiting surface reports "cross-platform nightly red since 2026-09-18, 2 nights" citing run 35438189645. Every cross-platform run in the last day has been PR-triggered rather than the cron, so that line may be reporting the last CRON run rather than current state. Worth a glance — a staleness bug in the red-nightly indicator would be PRIN-4's class in the surface we use to notice PRIN-4 problems.
